executive_summary.overall_assessment: PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED — Strong engineering culture with deterministic architecture tests and banned-API enforcement, but missing the formal Harness framework structure: no HARNESS.md, no verification slots, no three loops, no entropy/GC mechanisms, and no CI workflows in-repo.
implemented: Deterministic architecture layering tests (46 tests, NetArchTest + reflection)
BannedSymbols.txt enforced by RS0030 analyzer at build time
7 Roslyn analyzer packages wired solution-wide in Directory.Build.props
DI lifetime analyzers (DI001–DI027) with error-severity on captive deps
Comprehensive documentation ecosystem (~35 docs, ADRs, DECISIONS.md)
ROP (Result<T>) pattern enforced by BannedSymbols.txt GetResult() bans
Zero-unsafe blocks enforced at project level
Post-change check scripts for UI hygiene
missing_critical: HARNESS.md — the single source of truth for constraints
Verification slots — uniform interface for deterministic + agent checks
Three enforcement loops (inner/middle/outer) — no explicit mechanism
GitHub Actions CI workflows (not present in-repo)
Supply-chain pinning (NU1603 suppressed, no exact-version policy)

detailed_findings.title: No HARNESS.md — constraints are scattered
detailed_findings.description: Harness Engineering requires a HARNESS.md as the central constraint document readable by both humans and agents. Harbor has AGENTS.md (operational) and CLAUDE.md (conventions), but no unified constraints file. Constraints exist across BannedSymbols.txt, ARCHITECTURE_LAYERS.md, ANALYZERS.md, and .editorconfig with no single authoritative index.
evidence: No HARNESS.md found at repo root or anywhere in the tree
AGENTS.md (777 lines) focuses on operational guidance, not enforceable constraints
CLAUDE.md (1197 lines) encodes conventions but has no constraint registry or verification slot model
Constraints are split across 5+ files: BannedSymbols.txt, ARCHITECTURE_LAYERS.md, ANALYZERS.md, .editorconfig, DECISIONS.md
detailed_findings.recommendation: Create HARNESS.md with sections: (1) constraint catalog with verification slots (deterministic/agent/manual), (2) promotion ladder for constraint maturity, (3) GC rules, (4) three-loop enforcement map. Link from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.

detailed_findings.title: Documentation is comprehensive but not harness-shaped
detailed_findings.description: Harbor has ~35 docs, ADRs, and multiple markdown files providing excellent context. However, they are not structured as a living harness with agent-readable constraint blocks, hook-ready snippets, or verification slots.
evidence: docs/ contains 60+ files including PATTERNS.md, ANTIPATTERNS.md, EXAMPLES.md, CODE_PRINCIPLES_AUDIT.md
DECISIONS.md has 8 ADRs with dates and consequences
.ai-factory/DESCRIPTION.md exists but is an AI-factory config, not a harness doc
No YAML frontmatter constraints, no verification slot markers, no hook-ready constraint blocks
detailed_findings.recommendation: Add a docs/harness/ or .harness/ directory with constraint YAML/JSON that agents and CI can consume. Convert key conventions into machine-readable constraint blocks.

detailed_findings.title: Deterministic architecture enforcement exists and is strong
detailed_findings.description: Harbor has one of the strongest deterministic constraint systems examined: 46 architecture tests (21 reflection + 25 NetArchTest), BannedSymbols.txt enforced by RS0030, 7 analyzer packages, DI lifetime analyzers with error severity, and TreatWarningsAsErrors.
evidence: tests/Harbor.Architecture.Tests/ — 46 tests covering 47/50 src directories
Directory.Build.props wires: Roslynator, SonarAnalyzer, NetAnalyzers, AsyncFixer, ReflectionAnalyzers, BannedApiAnalyzers, Meziantou.Analyzer, DI.Lifetime.Analyzers
BannedSymbols.txt (68 lines) with RS0030 enforcement and documented exemptions
TreatWarningsAsErrors=true at solution level
Deterministic=true in Directory.Build.props
detailed_findings.recommendation: None — this is exemplary. Document this as the 'deterministic layer' in HARNESS.md and add CI workflow files to actually run these checks on PR.

detailed_findings.title: No GitHub Actions CI workflows in-repo
detailed_findings.description: The repo has no .github/workflows/ directory. CI is described in docs/BUILD.md and docs/CI_UI_TESTS.md as YAML examples, but no actual workflow files exist. This means none of the deterministic checks run automatically on PR.
evidence: find .github -type f returned empty
docs/BUILD.md contains a YAML example marked '# .github/workflows/build.yml' but it is not present
docs/CI_UI_TESTS.md contains CI step examples but no actual workflow
tools/post-change-check.sh exists but is manual/opt-in
detailed_findings.recommendation: Create .github/workflows/build.yml with: (1) dotnet build with analyzers, (2) per-project test loop, (3) architecture tests, (4) UI hygiene gate, (5) banned-API check. This is the #1 gap blocking the 'living harness'.

detailed_findings.title: Agent-enforced constraints dominate soft rules
detailed_findings.description: Many critical architectural rules are enforced only by code review and agent discipline (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md), not by deterministic tools. Examples: composition-root DI registration, interface segregation, value object placement, and cross-reference avoidance.
evidence: CLAUDE.md §Soft rules explicitly states 'code-review-enforced — not mechanically checkable'
Concrete impl types must be new'd only in HostBuilder.cs — no analyzer enforces this
New interfaces must go in Harbor.Abstractions — convention only
Application projects must not cross-reference — no NetArchTest rule found for this
detailed_findings.recommendation: Add Roslyn analyzers or extend NetArchTest rules to cover soft rules. For example: (1) forbid 'new' on concrete types outside HostBuilder/Modules, (2) forbid interfaces in Harbor.Core, (3) add cross-reference tests for Application layer projects.

detailed_findings.title: No scheduled entropy checks or GC mechanisms
detailed_findings.description: Harness Engineering requires periodic entropy-fighting checks (dependency audit, constraint drift, dead docs, stale ADRs). Harbor has none of these automated or scheduled.
evidence: No cron jobs, scheduled workflows, or entropy-check scripts found
No govulncheck, dotnet audit, or SBOM generation in build scripts
FEATURE_RESEARCH.md mentions 'supply-chain hardening' as a future need (no equivalent policy for NuGet)
No auto-fix safety rubric or entropy-fighting patterns documented
detailed_findings.recommendation: Add: (1) Weekly GitHub Action running dependency audit (dotnet list package --vulnerable, govulncheck), (2) Monthly ADR staleness check, (3) docs/GC.md with entropy-fighting rules and auto-fix safety rubric.

detailed_findings.title: Supply-chain pinning missing
detailed_findings.description: Harbor uses Central Package Management but suppresses NU1603 (Package version not found) and does not pin transitive dependencies. The Harness framework expects exact-version pinning with an allowlist for lifecycle scripts.
evidence: Directory.Build.props: <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);NU1603</NoWarn>
CentralPackageTransitivePinningEnabled=true but no exact-pinning policy documented
FEATURE_RESEARCH.md explicitly notes: 'Harbor has no equivalent policy for NuGet'
No PackageAudit or SBOM tooling in build scripts
detailed_findings.recommendation: Remove NU1603 suppression, enable transitive pinning strictly, add dotnet audit / govulncheck to CI, generate SBOM on release.

detailed_findings.title: No progressive hardening map
detailed_findings.description: The framework requires mapping each constraint to its verification state (unverified / agent-enforced / deterministic). Harbor has deterministic and agent-enforced constraints but no explicit map showing which is which or a promotion ladder.
evidence: No file or section mapping constraints to enforcement tiers
ANALYZERS.md lists what is deterministic but does not catalog agent-only constraints
CLAUDE.md 'Soft rules' are implicitly agent-enforced but not labeled as such
No promotion ladder for upgrading agent rules to deterministic
detailed_findings.recommendation: Add a Progressive Hardening table to HARNESS.md: columns for Constraint, Current State, Verification Slot, Promotion Path. Start with a constraint catalog extracted from existing docs.

detailed_findings.title: Three loops not explicitly implemented
detailed_findings.description: Harness Engineering defines inner loop (edit-time hooks), middle loop (CI/agent review), and outer loop (scheduled entropy checks). Harbor has fragments of all three but no unified mechanism.
evidence: Inner loop: tools/post-change-check.sh and code-inspect.sh exist but are manual scripts, not IDE hooks
Middle loop: CI is documented but not present; architecture tests exist but don't run on PR; no agent-based review agent found
Outer loop: No scheduled jobs, no entropy checks, no reflection log
detailed_findings.recommendation: Document the three loops in HARNESS.md and implement: (1) inner loop via pre-tool hooks or a watcher, (2) middle loop via actual GitHub Actions CI, (3) outer loop via scheduled weekly GitHub Actions workflow for entropy checks.

detailed_findings.title: No agent team / compound learning pipeline
detailed_findings.description: The framework expects an agent team (reviewer, implementer, QA, etc.) and a REFLECTION_LOG.md for compound learning. Harbor has no agent definitions or reflection mechanism.
evidence: No agents/ directory or agent markdown files
No REFLECTION_LOG.md
No MODEL_ROUTING.md for model-tier guidance
No skills/ directory with project-local skills
detailed_findings.recommendation: Add .harness/agents/ with minimal agent specs (reviewer, qa-check, architecture-enforcer) and create REFLECTION_LOG.md template. This is optional for 'harness-only' setup but required for full habitat.

detailed_findings.title: No verification slot abstraction
detailed_findings.description: Harness Engineering's verification slot model provides a uniform interface for deterministic and agent-based checks. Harbor has deterministic checks (tests, analyzers) and agent checks (code review) but no unified slot mechanism.
evidence: No verification slot YAML/JSON in repo
No constraint registry with checker metadata
Analyzers and tests are wired through MSBuild/TUnit directly, not through a harness-aware interface
detailed_findings.recommendation: Create .harness/verification-slots/ with YAML entries: id, scope, type (deterministic|agent|manual), command, on-failure. Reference from HARNESS.md.

detailed_findings.title: Strong agent documentation but no executable agent pipeline
detailed_findings.description: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are thorough and actively used. However, they are passive documents — there is no agent-based enforcement pipeline (no harness-enforcer agent, no constraint-checking subagent, no CUPID review agent).
evidence: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are high quality but static
No agent markdown files in repo
No ai-literacy-superpowers plugin installed (no HARNESS.md hooks)
Code review is human-only; no automated agent review on PR
detailed_findings.recommendation: Install the ai-literacy-superpowers plugin or create local agent specs. At minimum, add a harness-enforcer agent that reads HARNESS.md and runs deterministic + agent checks through a unified interface.

detailed_findings.title: BannedSymbols.txt and analyzers are well-maintained
detailed_findings.description: The banned-API system is production-grade: 68-line catalog, RS0030 analyzer, documented exemptions with reasons, and CI-ready build failure on violations.
evidence: BannedSymbols.txt with Newtonsoft, sync-over-async, Thread.Sleep bans
Exemptions catalogued by class with #pragma reasons
RS0030 wired in Directory.Build.props as AdditionalFiles
Legacy exemptions are limited and justified
detailed_findings.recommendation: None — keep current. Consider adding a CI gate that diffs BannedSymbols.txt additions to catch scope creep.

detailed_findings.title: ROP enforcement via banned APIs is effective
detailed_findings.description: The framework's Railway Oriented Programming requirement is enforced by banning .GetResult() and .GetAwaiter().GetResult() via BannedSymbols.txt, making sync-over-async a build failure in production code.
evidence: BannedSymbols.txt bans TaskAwaiter.GetResult and ValueTaskAwaiter.GetResult (generic and non-generic)
ConfigurableTaskAwaitable variants also banned
Exemptions limited to composition-root and UI-thread-marshaling contexts
detailed_findings.recommendation: None — this is a model example of turning a convention into a deterministic constraint.

detailed_findings.title: NUKE build system exists but CI is not configured
detailed_findings.description: The repo has a NUKE build system (build.sh, build/_build.csproj, .nuke/) and tooling scripts, but no actual CI pipeline runs these automatically on push/PR.
evidence: build/build.sh boots NUKE and supports Compile, Test, etc.
.nuke/ contains build binaries and temp logs
tools/ has post-change-check.sh, code-inspect.sh, ui-hygiene.sh
No .github/workflows/ found
detailed_findings.recommendation: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml that invokes NUKE or directly runs dotnet build/test per-project. Include architecture tests, UI tests, and banned-API validation.

detailed_findings.title: Decision archaeology is strong (8 ADRs)
detailed_findings.description: DECISIONS.md contains 8 ADRs with status, context, decision, and consequences. This supports the framework's decision archaeology discipline.
evidence: ADR-001 through ADR-008 in DECISIONS.md
Each ADR has status, date range, git log references, and consequences
docs/adr/ directory exists with 7 additional ADR markdown files
Cross-referenced from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md
detailed_findings.recommendation: None — excellent. Ensure HARNESS.md cross-references ADRs and promotes decision archaeology into the constraint review process.

framework_component.notes: Deterministic checks exist but not through uniform slots
